items.title: No local measure of missed care
items.whyItMatters: Budget decisions and union claims rest on anecdote.
items.opportunity: Measure last-shift missed care on all 18 units in one window.

items.title: Staffing and acuity are entangled
items.whyItMatters: Published results conflict on whether acuity explains the association (claims c1, c2, c3).
items.opportunity: Link each response to the actual hours and the acuity of the shift described and report both unadjusted and acuity-adjusted estimates.

items.title: The checklist is not validated for licensed practical nurses
items.whyItMatters: No instrument has been validated for this group (claim c5), which is about a third of the workforce.
items.opportunity: Cognitive pretest with eight licensed practical nurses and report the two roles separately.

items.title: Night and part-time staff respond less
items.whyItMatters: Reminder-based surveys over-represent day and full-time nurses (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Use the union's paid time on every shift type and report response by shift and role.

items.title: Results could be used to blame individuals
items.whyItMatters: Small units at night could make responses identifiable.
items.opportunity: Report only cells with five or more responses and agree a reporting rule with the union and management before fielding.

errorsFound: The member report and the conference abstract carry no year and cannot be appraised; they are kept unrated rather than given a quality score.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a cross-sectional last-shift survey linked to shift-level staffing and acuity, with role-specific reporting and a pre-agreed non-blaming reporting rule.
summary: Five gaps; missing local data and the staffing-acuity entanglement are high severity.
